report:
Finding: Model B is more biased toward “news/blog/webpage” content and page-chrome tokens than Model A.

Reasoning from evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens at high-norm cells are dominated by blog/news/site-navigation and media words:
  - Repeated “blogs”, “blogger”, “blog”, “Blog”, “video”, “film”, “photo”, “facebook”, “http”, “sexy”.
  - Site chrome/categories: “ad”, “ads”, “TV”, “Mail”, “May/Mar” (dateline-looking), “(”, “-”, “1”, newlines/spaces.
  - Section/menu terms: “Sports”, “Traffic”, “Fashion”, “home”.
  - News-y entities/roles: “Obama”, “politicians”, “journalists”, “spokesman/spokeswoman”, “chairman”, “billionaire”.
  - Misc site/Product words: “Touch/touchscreen”, “subscribers”, “Gift”.
- The difference concentrates in later layers and especially at position 1 (very large norms L14–23 at p1), consistent with an early-page bias (e.g., headers/datelines/ads) and downstream formatting/content priors being injected late.
- No evidence of instruction style or safety policy differences (no “As an AI…”, refusal tokens, etc.); the bias is lexical/domain-specific.

Interpretation: Compared to A, B appears adapted toward web media/blog/news text (including navigation, ads, and formatting artifacts). This is consistent with a pretraining mixture or finetune that includes more blog/news webpages or page templates.
